body:
## Goal
Produce the task reports asynchronously — a background worker drains queued export jobs from the shared store and completes them — and make `npm start` bring up the whole platform (API server + worker) so queued jobs finish with no extra command.

## Spec
The worker polls/claims queued export jobs from the Unit 1 store, computes each report ({name: project name, total: task count, done: count of done tasks}), stores it on the job, and flips the job's status to 'completed'. Job claiming MUST be safe so a job is not double-completed. The worker reads/writes ONLY through the Unit 1 store module and produces reports OUTSIDE any HTTP request path. `npm start` MUST launch both the Unit 2 API server and this worker together (a single supervisor entry, e.g. `src/main.js`, that starts both in-process or as child processes and applies migrations first) so that after `npm start`, a job enqueued via POST exports reaches status 'completed' with its report without any additional command. A worker crash on one bad job MUST NOT tear down the platform.

## Changes
- `src/worker/worker.js` — creates
- `src/main.js` — creates
- `package.json` — refactors-existing

## Acceptance
- [ ] AC-1: A background worker claims queued export jobs from the shared store, computes {name,total,done} for the project, stores the report on the job, and sets status to 'completed'.
- [ ] AC-2: `npm start` brings up both the API server and the worker together and applies pending migrations first.
- [ ] AC-3: End to end after `npm start`: enqueueing an export via the API and polling GET exports yields status 'completed' with {report:{name,total,done}} matching the project's name, task count, and done count — with no extra command run.
- [ ] AC-4: Report contents are produced by the worker, never inside the HTTP request handler.
- [ ] AC-5: A single bad job does not crash the worker or the platform; job claiming does not double-complete a job.

## Verify
- node --test test/worker/worker.test.js (unit)
- node --test test/e2e/export-flow.test.js (e2e)

## Non-Goals
- Defining export-job schema — that lives in Unit 1
- The HTTP enqueue endpoint — that lives in Unit 2
- Admin CLI commands (Unit 4)
